combinations.magnitude: reduced at 30 and 60 min with combination vs 45 min with morphine alone; female only
combinations.evidence_quote: By contrast, in females, morphine (1 mg/kg) decreased mechanical hypersensitivity at 45 minutes after injection when given alone, and at 30 and 60 minutes after injection when given in combination with pioglitazone [Fig 4B; F (2, 19) = 4.712 P=0.0218, Table 1 lines #49–51].

combinations.magnitude: no change alone or combined in males
combinations.evidence_quote: In males, morphine (1 mg/kg) did not change mechanical hypersensitivity when given alone or in combination with 10 mg/kg pioglitazone [Fig 4A; P>0.05, Table 1 lines #46–48].

combinations.magnitude: tended to decrease at 15 min; female only
combinations.evidence_quote: In females, the combination of morphine with pioglitazone tended to decrease cold hypersensitivity 15 minutes after intraperitoneal injection [Fig 4E; Table 1 lines #58–60].

combinations.magnitude: no change alone or combined in males
combinations.evidence_quote: In males, morphine (1 mg/kg) did not change mechanical hypersensitivity when given alone or in combination with 10 mg/kg pioglitazone [Fig 4D; P>0.05, Table 1 lines #55–57].
